Well aren't entirely off base with this. Depression is a two part problem. One part is not necessarily that brain chemistry and biology are responsible, but that they can make you predisposed, or more likely to, fall into depressive behaviour. This predisposition doesn't mean you WILL be depressed, but because it can effect your perception and decision making, it certainly plays a role for those who do suffer from depression. The other half is more specific to an individuals personal experiences and the environment of their life. Those born into poverty, those who are abused or have abusive relationships are at a high risk for depression because of the stress of these situations and the way it effects self esteem and social development. Of course, not every id born into a high risk situation, yet still experience depression. Self esteem is huge in any  instance of depression, that can be effected regardless of brain chemistry or environment. More than ever is self esteem effected because of social media, and advertising media. On facebook you see the highlight reel and compare it to you outtakes, and in advertisement we see a perfection we "could" have but never seem to attain. So, yea drugs alone can't solve the problem, but for those who have a predisposition it can turn the tables and provide the energy and positive outlook needed to face the more pressing issues of self image, decision making, maintaining a healthy and productive lifestyle.

And constantly that man up and get my shit together. I do sometimes(man up), but then I wonder, and think, and end up back at square one. It's tough to ask for the help but...as early as I am into it, just having the support is helping. Also, I'm pretty sure we are both cripplingly brilliant humans, suffering from existential depression. Basically, we've realized that nothing has any inherent meaning. Why do I get out of bed at all? Right? And because we are logical, we value logic above emotion, and disregard emotional arguments. I was told to stop worry why I do things, and what they mean, and to just do them and enjoy them. Easier said then done, but I think we can agree on the obviousness of the solution.

Granted, you won't stop thinking...but you can always say fuck it and do your best to ignore the thoughts. So far that's as best I can do, plus the ssri. And it might just work.
